title: 3dfx Voodoo Graphics Card
summary: The groundbreaking 3D add-on accelerator card utilizing the Glide API that catalyzed the 3D PC gaming hardware revolution.
facts: Came with 4MB of EDO DRAM (2MB frame buffer, 2MB texture memory).
Required a passthrough VGA cable connected to an existing 2D graphics card.
Offered unprecedented hardware bilinear filtering, anti-aliasing, and alpha blending.

title: Intel Pentium Processor (P5 / P54C)
summary: Superscalar x86 processor introduced by Intel featuring dual execution pipelines, 64-bit data bus, and floating-point unit (FPU).
facts: First Intel x86 CPU to use a brand name instead of a number sequence (e.g. 586) to secure trademark protection.
Famous for the 1994 Pentium FDIV floating-point division bug that caused a major recall.
Introduced Pentium MMX technology in 1997 with 57 new SIMD instructions for multimedia.

title: Creative Sound Blaster 16
summary: The de facto industry standard PC audio card for 16-bit 44.1kHz CD-quality digital sound and Yamaha OPL3 FM synthesis in DOS/Windows games.
facts: Offered 16-bit stereo CD-quality audio playback and recording.
Included Yamaha YMF262 (OPL3) chip for retro FM synth game music.
Featured a 15-pin gameport joystick connector and optional ASP/CSP digital signal processor slot.

title: Intel Pentium II Processor
summary: Sixth-generation x86 microprocessor packaged in a distinctive Single Edge Contact Cartridge (SECC) for Slot 1 mainboards.
facts: Built on P6 microarchitecture inherited from Pentium Pro.
Housed the CPU die and 512KB off-die L2 cache on a PCB cartridge with plastic casing.
Operated at clock speeds ranging from 233 MHz to 450 MHz.

title: Cyrix 6x86 Processor
summary: Popular budget alternative Socket 7 CPU boasting superior integer math performance over Intel Pentium at lower prices.
facts: Used P-rating system (e.g. 6x86 PR166+) indicating integer equivalence to Pentium clock speeds.
Suffered from weak floating-point unit (FPU) performance in games like Quake.
Designed by Cyrix and manufactured in IBM and SGS-Thomson semiconductor foundries.
